title: Process monitoring
subtitle: See and stop processes — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Live, dynamically updating process list (CPU, memory, PID, user, command)
cards.notes: Refreshes until you quit. Load averages and memory summary sit at the top; the table is the process list. Dashboard, not a one-shot snapshot.

cards.example: press q while top is running
cards.notes: Leaves the live UI. Memory hook: top = dashboard; q to leave.

cards.meaning: Sort process list by CPU usage
cards.notes: Useful when hunting a CPU hog. Contrast with M (sort by memory).

cards.meaning: Sort process list by memory usage
cards.notes: Use when RAM pressure is the question. Contrast with P (sort by CPU).

cards.meaning: Kill a process from inside top (asks for PID and signal)
cards.example: press k, enter PID, choose signal
cards.notes: Interactive kill without leaving top. Still need the PID from the table.

cards.meaning: One-shot snapshot of processes: all users, user-oriented columns, including daemons
cards.notes: Frozen photo, not a movie. Columns include USER, PID, %CPU, %MEM, STAT, COMMAND — use PID with kill.

cards.meaning: Show processes of all users (not only yours)
cards.notes: BSD-style flag. Combined with u and x in the classic ps aux.
Makes the snapshot readable for who owns what and how much they use.

cards.meaning: Include processes with no controlling terminal (daemons)
cards.notes: Without x you miss background services. Memory hook: ps aux = everyone, including daemons.

cards.meaning: Find PIDs by matching the command name in the snapshot
cards.notes: Careful: grep often matches itself too. Prefer kill PID once you have the number.

cards.meaning: Send SIGTERM (15) — polite request to exit cleanly
cards.notes: Default signal is TERM. Cannot kill another user’s process unless you are root. Need the number from ps/top.

cards.meaning: Send SIGKILL — force stop; process cannot catch or ignore it
cards.notes: Same as kill -KILL. Use when TERM is ignored. Does not run cleanup (temp files; children may remain). Shotgun, not ask.

cards.meaning: SIGTERM every process with that command name
cards.notes: Dangerous on a busy box: killall java kills every Java. Prefer kill PID when you mean one process.

cards.meaning: SIGKILL every process with that command name
cards.notes: Same force as kill -9, but by name. killall -KILL top is equivalent (signal by name, not number).
